item.text: The reconnaissance establishes a high-information but access-constrained environment: formal federal authority is clear, while conflict zones and Tigray communications/access were deliberately restricted. I’m now consolidating reusable claims across chapters, keeping country-level indicators as context and reserving ruler attribution for documented federal decisions, conduct, or formal authority.

Research pass completed for Abiy Ahmed, Ethiopia, 2022. No score or score range was assigned.

The requested files could not be written because the workspace is read-only; the complete handoff is below.

## Authority and evidence environment

- **E001 — Formal authority:** Ethiopia’s prime minister holds the highest federal executive power, chairs the Council of Ministers, commands the armed forces, and nominates senior Supreme Court officials. This supports federal attribution, while preserving limits from Ethiopia’s federal structure. [Office of the Prime Minister](https://pmo.gov.et/government/).
- **E002 — Information environment:** Media space was more open than under the prior government, but RSF reports polarization, government narrative control, and regulatory pressure on dissenting journalism. [RSF Ethiopia 2022](https://rsf.org/en/analyse_regionale/817).
- **E003 — Conflict visibility:** Amnesty and HRW documented communications blackouts and restricted physical access, making silence weak evidence and increasing underreporting risk. [Amnesty](https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/afr25/5777/2022/en/), [HRW](https://www.hrw.org/news/2022/04/06/ethiopia-crimes-against-humanity-western-tigray-zone).

## Evidence register

- **E004 — Western Tigray abuses:** HRW/Amnesty documented killings, sexual violence, arbitrary detention, pillage, forcible transfer, denial of aid, and the expulsion of several hundred thousand Tigrayans. Federal acquiescence or participation was possible but not established as a personal order. [HRW report](https://www.hrw.org/news/2022/04/06/ethiopia-crimes-against-humanity-western-tigray-zone).
- **E005 — Broader conflict and accountability:** HRW reports abuses by all parties, emergency powers, Tigray’s continuing internet shutdown, minimal accountability, and pressure against independent investigations. [HRW World Report 2022](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2022/country-chapters/ethiopia).
- **E006 — Political/media constraints:** Freedom House and RSF document opposition intimidation, restricted reporting, emergency powers, shutdowns, and a mixed record of earlier liberalization. [Freedom House](https://freedomhouse.org/country/ethiopia/freedom-world/2022), [Freedom on the Net](https://freedomhouse.org/country/ethiopia/freedom-net/2022).
- **E007 — 2022 peace process:** The Pretoria agreement was identified in discovery, but the retrieved copy was only a gateway and was not accepted as final evidence pending canonical source validation.
- **E008 — Peace implementation and reforms:** The World Bank recorded Abiy’s December 2022 discussion of implementing the peace agreement, health and flood grants, early-childhood education, human capital, exchange-rate reform, SOEs, and private-sector growth. [World Bank](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/statement/2022/12/14/readout-from-world-bank-group-president-david-malpasss-meeting-with-prime-minister-abiy-ahmed-of-ethiopia).
- **E009 — Macro reform and shocks:** IMF staff recorded inflation, fiscal and external pressures from multiple shocks, alongside government commitments to private-sector growth, SOE oversight, FX reform, and debt sustainability. [IMF](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2022/06/21/pr22216-ethiopia-imf-staff-visit-discusses-reform-plans-and-economic-developments-in-ethiopia).
- **E010 — Education systems:** A 2022 World Bank education expenditure and institutional review was located, but substantive findings were not retrievable from the page; retained as context only. [World Bank PEIR](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099615206172211408).
- **E011 — Drought and health response:** UN reporting describes five failed rainy seasons, severe food insecurity affecting roughly 24 million people in southern and southeastern Ethiopia, and WHO-supported mobile health and nutrition services. [United Nations in Ethiopia](https://ethiopia.un.org/en/221722-delivering-health-services-ethiopia%E2%80%99s-drought-affected-populations).
- **E012 — Humanitarian environment:** UNICEF records northern conflict, inter-ethnic conflict, and the worst drought in forty years affecting Afar, Oromia, and Somali. [UNICEF 2022 report](https://www.unicef.org/ethiopia/reports/annual-report-2022).
- **E013 — Agricultural interventions:** A 2022 FAO paper associates agricultural interventions with higher yields and improved food security, with heterogeneous effects benefiting vulnerable households. It does not establish Abiy’s personal responsibility. [FAO](https://www.fao.org/agrifood-economics/publications/detail/en/c/1622675/).
- **E014 — Wheat procurement:** A UNOPS wheat-procurement page was discovered but could not be fetched; excluded from defensible evidence.
- **E015 — Anti-corruption agenda:** Transparency International records Abiy’s governance-reform promise and post-November 2022 anti-corruption focus, but no personal integrity finding. [Transparency International](https://knowledgehub.transparency.org/country/ethiopia).
- **E016 — Direct reform agenda:** The World Bank meeting provides direct evidence of Abiy’s policy agenda, but not independent implementation or outcome proof.

## Local structured baseline

- **1B:** No local nuclear/existential-risk facts. No inference of safety, non-exposure, or inapplicability.
- **2B:** Local UCDP facts show 697 state-based conflict events and 101,076 fatalities in 2022; SIPRI shows roughly $1.01bn military spending. These measure exposure and burden, not personal initiation or legality.
- **3B:** Local target-year indicators show severe physical-integrity and repression concerns, including 1,821 one-sided-violence deaths and 378 government-actor killings. Warnings prohibit automatic personal attribution.
- **4B:** Local indicators show weak political-freedom context: Freedom House civil liberties 6, political rights 5; V-Dem electoral democracy 0.30, expression 0.354, rule of law 0.341; RSF score 50.53.
- **5B:** Local GDP, income, consumption, capital formation, and productivity facts show economic growth context but contain attribution and nominal-price caveats.
- **6B:** Local HDI was 0.492; life expectancy 65.645 years; expected schooling 9.94 years; DTP3/HepB3 coverage 63%; under-five mortality 49.52 per 1,000. These are outcomes, not proof of policy contribution.
- **7B:** Local corruption indicators are country-level only. No personal nexus was established for truthfulness, assets, favoritism, appointments, concealment, or obstruction.
- **8B:** Local government-effectiveness and outcome indicators provide context, not evidence of Abiy’s program execution or adaptation.

## Chapter yield and gaps

- **1B:** No defensible ruler-specific evidence retained. Need nuclear, cyber, biological, dual-use, and catastrophic-risk research.
- **2B:** Strongest evidence concerns conflict harm, federal/regional attribution limits, and the 2022 peace process. Need validated Pretoria text, implementation evidence, civilian-protection records, and accountability outcomes.
- **3B:** Strong evidence of severe conflict-related physical harm and restricted scrutiny. Need target-year investigations, remedies, prosecutions, and non-Tigray vulnerable-group evidence.
- **4B:** Reusable evidence covers media opening, narrative control, emergency powers, opposition constraints, and shutdowns. Need direct 2022 legal, electoral, judicial, and opposition records.
- **5B:** Reform agenda and macroeconomic pressures are documented. Need budgets, implementation, appointments, distributional outcomes, inflation management, and correction evidence.
- **6B:** Drought, conflict, food insecurity, health response, and human-capital agendas are documented. Need service quality, equity, affordability, donor attribution, and institutional durability.
- **7B:** No defensible personal-integrity evidence. Country corruption indicators remain context only. Need financial, legal, appointment, disclosure, and scrutiny records.
- **8B:** Reform, peace, human-capital, and agricultural programs are identifiable, but the implementation-to-outcome chain remains incomplete.

The research used English-language sources only. Local-language archives and reporting in Amharic, Oromo, Tigrinya, and Arabic remain gaps.
